chapter: Brown's Band in Chicago and New York
title: Celebrity visitors and refusing Joe Levy's contract
summary: Stars like Irene Castle visited; Loyacano alone refused to sign a contract with agent Joe Levy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: it got to be an attraction, whereas one performer would ask the other if he heard that band over there. And they'd say, no, it's a go over here. Oh yeah, heavy Berlin and what's the name of these uh, dancers. Oh, it's right on the tip of my tongue right now. They were the big time dancers of all time around that. Man? No, uh, man and his wife. I remember her, Castle, Irene Castle. Uh huh. She used to come in there with a monkey on her shoulder, live monkey. And they danced a couple of times to the music and they said it was great. Well, we could have went with them, but who wanted to go? Nobody wanted to go. It wouldn't have been any better anyhow, because by that time, uh, everybody signed up except me to a contract. And I didn't want anybody to sign a contract because they said, these guys are smarter than you are. That fella named Joe Levy was booking agent. He gave a long syrupy talk, you know, and I was the only one who didn't sign a contract. I can prove that. The rest of them signed a contract. Sure, he offered us too much. I mean, uh, to leave that and go to New York, you mean? No, no, he, uh, uh, he, he, he would give us so much more money a week each three months. And we could do this and we could do that. And when it come time to sign the contract, read the contract, I guess I was the only one who read it. He was offering us nothing. So I said, well, I can do better without a contract. And that way I figured I could make him look up to me instead of me looking down to him. See? So, uh, because I, we weren't in a union at that time and I could quit on a moment's notice. And if I quit, then the band was hooked. No piano player, they couldn't play, that was for sure. Yeah, nobody up there was playing that style at all? Oh, no, no. Never heard of it.
